title: (No AI) Meta removes language that may have allowed it to scrape news sites
author: Terrence O’Brien
content:
![Image of the Meta logo and wordmark on a blue background bordered by black scribbles made out of the Meta logo.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/02/STK043_VRG_Illo_N_Barclay_2_Meta.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

After backlash, Meta is [updating its terms again](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1012846/meta-business-terms-scrape-news-publishers) to remove language that suggested it could scrape content from sites, including news sites, to train its AI. Specifically, the following language no longer appears on the [commercial terms page](https://www.facebook.com/legal/commercial_terms_preview):

> … Meta may use any content from such domains, web pages, or URLs to provide, develop, improve, research, train, and maintain the integrity of, the Meta Company Products, services, and features provided under these Commercial Terms and any other applicable supplemental terms.

Many, including _[Neiman Lab](https://www.niemanlab.org/2026/10/metas-new-commercial-terms-will-allow-the-scraping-of-news-sites-legal-experts-say/)_ and James Grimmelmann, a professor of digital and information law at Cornell, interpreted it as an …

title: (No AI) Websites are closing their doors to AI agents
author: Emma Roth
content:
![Digital collage of various toy robots.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/03/STK414_AI_CVIRGINIA_C.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Autonomous agents are the hottest thing in AI. OpenAI, Meta, Google, Instinct, and others promise their agents can scour the internet on your behalf, doing anything from booking a dinner reservation and cleaning out your inbox to buying new shoes. But what happens when the rest of the internet won't play nice?

In recent weeks, users of services like Meta's Muse, xAI's Grok, OpenAI's Dots, and Instinct have reported blocks preventing their AI agents from performing tasks across top websites. Yelp [told _TechCrunch_](https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/06/the-next-hurdle-for-ai-agents-getting-websites-to-let-them-in/) that it only allows AI agents that pay for its data licensing program, while Delta Air Lines is preventing them from booking ticket …

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1013195/ai-agents-blocked-web)
